html:
SMTO-CFG-0006 — The Gateway knows the SMTO address but not its port

GUID: f9b74175-9dbf-42f3-9918-fc2f50210b74
Slug: gateway-config-gateway-server-port-is-required-when-gateway
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer) was told which computer runs SMTO, but not which port to connect to. It stopped before starting, so it can't connect yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find SMTO's port: it is the number after the last colon in the web address you use to open SMTO. If there is no number, it is 443 for an https address. The Gateway connects to the same address and port that you use in your browser.
  2. If the Gateway is started with --server-host (-ServerHost on Windows), add --server-port (-ServerPort on Windows) followed by that number to the same start command. When the Gateway connects to SMTO itself, it needs both the address and the port.
  3. Otherwise, ask the person who set up the Gateway computer to set GATEWAY_SERVER_PORT to that number, or to clear GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST if SMTO should connect to the Gateway instead. Clearing the address makes the Gateway wait for SMTO to connect to it, so no port for SMTO is needed.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway starts and shows as Connected in Settings › Setup › Gateways.

If it still fails

  • Send the Gateway's startup message to the person who installed the Gateway. Don't try other port numbers at random; the Gateway can only connect on the port SMTO actually uses.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway Settings validation found GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST set (outbound mode) while GATEWAY_SERVER_PORT is unset or zero, leaving the Server connection address incomplete.

What this means

  • server_host is configured while server_port is zero or negative, leaving the outbound controller address incomplete. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • server_host is configured while server_port is zero or negative, leaving the outbound controller address incomplete.

How to diagnose it

  • Check GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST and GATEWAY_SERVER_PORT together on the outbound Gateway.

How to fix it

  • Set GATEWAY_SERVER_PORT (startup --server-port, or -ServerPort on Windows) to the Server's HTTPS port alongside GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST, with GATEWAY_SERVER_SCHEME=https, or clear GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST to run the Gateway in inbound mode, then restart it. The outbound Gateway connects to wss://host:port/api/agent/gateways/connect/ws and refuses a non-TLS ws URL, so the port must be the Server's TLS listener.
  • Supply the intended controller port from 1 through 65535 with GATEWAY_SERVER_HOST.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended configured controller has a valid nonzero port.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
